title: EKSU GST 115 - Introduction to Computer Application and Information Technology | Practice Bank

questions.stem: Which historical event is most directly linked to the early development of programmable computing devices like the Harvard Mark I?

options.B: The Cold War
options.C: World War II

questions.stem: In the context of computer generations, what technological advancement primarily characterized the second generation of computers?

options.B: Vacuum Tubes
options.C: Transistors

questions.stem: The concept of a "closed system" in computing implies which of the following about its interaction with the environment?

options.A: It actively exchanges information and energy with its surroundings.
options.B: It operates independently with minimal external influence.
options.C: It is designed to adapt its processes based on environmental feedback.
options.D: It is inherently unstable and prone to external disruption.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental characteristic of a "digital" computer system as opposed to an "analog" system?

options.B: It uses discrete numerical values for computation.
options.C: Its output is always an approximation of the input.
options.D: It is primarily used for measuring physical phenomena.

questions.stem: The development of UNIVAC I, a significant early electronic computer, is most closely associated with which of the following?

options.A: The need for advanced cryptography during wartime.
options.B: The automation of complex scientific calculations.
options.C: The processing of large volumes of census data.
options.D: The creation of early graphical user interfaces.

questions.stem: In the context of operating systems, what is the primary purpose of "context switching"?

options.A: To manage memory allocation for multiple applications.
options.B: To allow the CPU to switch between different tasks efficiently.
options.C: To provide a graphical interface for user interaction.
options.D: To ensure data integrity during file transfers.

questions.stem: The ".com" domain extension, commonly seen in web addresses, traditionally signifies a connection to which type of organization?

options.B: Government Agencies
options.C: Commercial Businesses

questions.stem: When discussing web navigation, what is the role of a "search engine"?

options.A: To display the content of a specific web page.
options.B: To translate web page code into a readable format.
options.C: To index and retrieve information from the World Wide Web.
options.D: To manage the connection between a user's computer and the internet.

questions.stem: The Shannon-Weaver communication model, when applied to information technology, identifies "noise" as a factor that:

options.A: Enhances the clarity of the message.
options.B: Distorts or interferes with the transmission of information.
options.C: Is a necessary component for encoding data.
options.D: Represents the intended meaning of the sender.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key characteristic of an "open system" in contrast to a "closed system"?

options.A: It is entirely self-contained and isolated.
options.B: It actively interacts and exchanges with its environment.
options.C: Its internal processes are completely predictable.
options.D: It is designed for minimal external dependencies.

questions.stem: The invention of the transistor during the second generation of computers led to significant improvements in:

options.B: The size and reliability of computing devices.
options.C: The development of graphical user interfaces.
options.D: The ability to perform complex mathematical operations.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of a "web browser"?

options.B: To translate human-readable text into binary code.
options.C: To access and display information from the World Wide Web.
options.D: To manage network connections between computers.

questions.stem: The term "information explosion" in the context of modern technology refers to:

options.A: The rapid increase in the volume and diversity of available information.
options.B: The sudden collapse of data storage systems.
options.C: A decrease in the speed of information dissemination.
options.D: The monopolization of information by a few entities.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary function of a "scheduler" in a multitasking operating system?

options.A: To manage hardware resources like printers.
options.B: To determine which process gets to use the CPU and for how long.
options.C: To encrypt sensitive user data.
options.D: To facilitate communication between different network devices.

questions.stem: The ".org" domain extension is typically associated with which type of entity?

options.B: Government Organizations
options.C: Non-profit Organizations

questions.stem: In the context of digital imaging, what device is used to convert a physical document or image into a digital format?

options.B: Scanner
options.C: Camera

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT considered a primary storage device?

options.B: RAM (Random Access Memory)
options.C: Solid State Drive

questions.stem: The development of the first electronic general-purpose computer, ENIAC, was a significant milestone during which historical period?

options.B: The Cold War
options.C: World War II

questions.stem: What does the acronym "TCP" stand for in the context of internet protocols?

options.B: Transmission Control Protocol
options.C: Technical Communication Protocol

questions.stem: MS Word, by default, saves documents in which file format?

options.B: .rtf
options.C: .docx

questions.stem: The term "GUI" is an acronym for what common computer interface concept?

options.B: Graphical User Interface
options.C: Global Utility Interface

questions.stem: Which of the following is a core function of a "database management system" (DBMS)?

options.B: Managing and organizing large amounts of data.
options.C: Editing video content.

questions.stem: The concept of "teleconferencing" primarily facilitates which type of communication?

options.B: Asynchronous text-based messaging.
options.C: Real-time audio and video interaction between multiple locations.

questions.stem: What does the acronym "DVD" commonly stand for?

options.B: Dynamic Versatile Disk
options.C: Digital Versatile Disc

questions.stem: In the context of the Shannon-Weaver model, the "source" is responsible for:

options.B: Encoding and transmitting the message.
options.C: Interpreting the message.

questions.stem: The term "web surfing" is a colloquialism for:

options.A: Downloading large files from the internet.
options.B: Navigating and exploring various websites on the World Wide Web.
options.C: Sending and receiving emails.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key characteristic of a "deterministic system"?

options.A: Its behavior is unpredictable and random.
options.B: Its future state is entirely determined by its current state and inputs.
options.C: It actively adapts to environmental changes.
options.D: It operates with a high degree of uncertainty.

questions.stem: The development of the third generation of computers was marked by the widespread adoption of which technology?

options.B: Vacuum Tubes
options.C: Integrated Circuits

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a "protocol" in computer networking?

options.A: To define the physical layout of network cables.
options.B: To establish a set of rules for communication between devices.
options.C: To encrypt all data transmitted over the network.
options.D: To manage the power supply to network hardware.

questions.stem: The term "hits" in the context of search engine results typically refers to:

options.A: The number of times a website has been visited.
options.B: The individual web pages that match a search query.
options.C: The speed at which a search engine processes queries.
options.D: The security measures employed by a search engine.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary function of an "email client" like Outlook Express?

options.B: To send, receive, and manage electronic mail.
options.C: To perform complex data analysis.

questions.stem: The concept of "information technology" (IT) encompasses which of the following?

options.A: Only the hardware components of computers.
options.B: The study and use of systems for storing, retrieving, and sending information.
options.C: Exclusively the software applications used for entertainment.
options.D: The physical infrastructure of telecommunication networks.

questions.stem: What does the acronym "FTP" stand for in networking?

options.B: Fast Transfer Protocol
options.C: File Transfer Protocol

questions.stem: The "1880 Census" is historically significant in the development of computing because it led to the application of which early data processing technology?

options.B: Electronic Calculators
options.C: Magnetic Tape Storage

questions.stem: A "cybernetic system" is characterized by its ability to:

options.A: Operate in complete isolation from its environment.
options.B: Maintain a stable internal state regardless of external conditions.
options.C: Regulate itself and interact with its environment to achieve goals.
options.D: Perform computations based on analog signals.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common example of an "application software" package?

options.B: A word processor
options.C: The CPU

questions.stem: The ability of a multitasking operating system to give the illusion of running multiple programs simultaneously is achieved through:

options.B: Context switching
options.C: Direct hardware manipulation

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of "HTML" in web development?

options.A: To define the network protocols for data transmission.
options.B: To structure and present content on web pages.
options.C: To encrypt sensitive information transmitted online.
options.D: To manage the flow of data between servers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of "analog" computer systems?

options.A: They process data using discrete numerical values.
options.B: They are primarily used for general-purpose computing.
options.C: They represent data using continuous physical quantities.
options.D: They are highly accurate for complex calculations.

questions.stem: The introduction of "microprocessors" is a defining characteristic of which generation of computers?

options.B: Second Generation
options.C: Third Generation

questions.stem: In the context of communication, what does "encoding" refer to?

options.A: The process of receiving and interpreting a message.
options.B: The conversion of a message into a transmittable form.
options.C: The introduction of errors into a message.
options.D: The physical medium used for transmission.

questions.stem: The term "information revolution" is often used to describe:

options.A: A period of decline in the availability of information.
options.B: The rapid and profound societal changes brought about by the widespread use of information technology.
options.C: The invention of the printing press.
options.D: The development of early forms of writing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental component of "Information and Communication Technology" (ICT) infrastructure?

options.B: Both hardware and software.
options.C: Only network cables.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the "Internet Protocol" (IP) in networking?

options.A: To define the syntax of web pages.
options.B: To provide unique addresses for devices on a network and route data packets.
options.C: To manage user authentication for websites.

questions.stem: Charles Babbage is credited with designing the first automatic calculating machine, known as the:

options.B: UNIVAC
options.C: Analytical Engine

questions.stem: The limitation of the UNIX operating system, as mentioned in the text, is its reliance on:

options.B: Command-line interface
options.C: Window-based operations

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a type of database management system (DBMS)?

options.B: MS Access
options.C: SQL Server

questions.stem: The "vacuum tube" was the primary electronic component used in which generation of computers?

options.B: Second Generation
options.C: Third Generation

questions.stem: The term "browser" in the context of the internet refers to:

options.A: A device for storing digital files.
options.B: A program used to access and view web pages.
options.C: A system for managing network connections.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of a "search engine" in relation to information retrieval on the internet?

options.A: To create and host web pages.
options.B: To provide a direct connection to any website.
options.C: To index and search vast amounts of online information.
options.D: To download files from the internet.

questions.stem: The concept of "socialization" as a function of communication in a social system, according to MacBride, relates to:

options.A: The dissemination of news and current events.
options.B: The process by which individuals learn and adopt societal norms and values.
options.C: The transmission of entertainment content.

questions.stem: What is the fundamental difference between "hardware" and "software" in computing?

options.A: Hardware is intangible, while software is physical.
options.B: Hardware refers to the physical components, while software refers to the instructions and programs.
options.C: Hardware is used for input, and software is used for output.
options.D: Hardware is always temporary, while software is permanent.

questions.stem: The term "universal access" in the context of communication technology implies:

options.A: Access only for a select few with specialized knowledge.
options.B: The ability for all individuals to access and utilize communication services.
options.C: Access limited to specific geographical regions.
options.D: Access that requires significant financial investment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common characteristic of a "portable document format" (PDF) file?

options.A: It can only be opened and edited by specific software.
options.B: It is designed to preserve document formatting across different platforms.
options.C: It is primarily used for creating animated graphics.
options.D: It is a temporary file format that is automatically deleted.

questions.stem: The invention of the "transistor" led to a significant reduction in the size and power consumption of computers, paving the way for which generation?

options.B: Second Generation
options.C: Third Generation

questions.stem: What is the primary role of a "channel" in the Shannon-Weaver communication model?

options.B: To introduce noise into the message.
options.C: The medium through which the message is transmitted.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the function of "context switching" in an operating system?

options.A: It allows the user to switch between different applications visually.
options.B: It enables the CPU to efficiently manage and switch between multiple running processes.
options.C: It is used to switch between different network protocols.
options.D: It is a security feature that switches user accounts.

questions.stem: The term "digital versatile disc" (DVD) highlights its capability to store:

options.B: Only video data.
options.C: Both audio and video data, as well as other digital information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental requirement for two computer systems to communicate effectively on a network?

options.A: They must have identical operating systems.
options.B: They must share a common set of communication protocols.
options.C: They must be physically connected by the same type of cable.
options.D: They must have the same brand of network card.

questions.stem: The concept of "information dissemination" in communication refers to:

options.A: The process of encoding a message.
options.B: The act of spreading or distributing information.
options.C: The interpretation of a message by the receiver.
